 At Gwalior

sentences.text: Shri B.D.Verma- Advocate for the respondents.

ORDER This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act has been filed by the appellant/Insurance Company, taking exception to the impugned award dated 23.10.2009 passed by the Fourth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Morena (M.P.) in Claim Case No.186/2008, whereby the Claims Tribunal has directed the Insurance Company to pay the compensation to the claimant and thereafter recover the same from owner and driver of the offending vehicle.

entities.text: Fourth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The date of the accident and the issue of negligence are not in dispute; however, the dispute pertains only to the liability.

3. As per the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in the case of injury to the claimant due to the motor accident, the Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.1,30,000/- along with interest.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant has filed the present appeal on the ground that at the time of the accident, the driver of the offending vehicle NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:333 2 MA-168-2010 was holding a valid and effective driving licence for a light motor vehicle (LMV), and National Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Dashrath Singh on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117568420/
1 the driving licence was not endorsed to permit him to drive a transport/commercial vehicle.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Dashrath Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, it is contended that the Claims Tribunal has committed an error in imposing liability upon the Insurance Company, and accordingly, setting aside of the impugned award against the Insurance Company is sought.
5.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents opposed the prayer and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

6. Heard the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.
It is not disputed that at the time of the accident, the driver of the offending Tata 207 was holding a licence to drive a light motor vehicle.
It is also not disputed that at the time of the accident, he was driving the offending vehicle, the weight of which was less than 7,500 kgs.

8. In this regard, reliance can be placed upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., AIR 2017 SC 3668, wherein the Apex Court has held as under:
"(ii) A transport vehicle and omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of either of which does not exceed 7,500 kg, would be a light motor vehicle and also motor car or tractor or a road roller, the 'unladen weight' of which does not exceed 7,500 kg; and the holder of a driving licence to drive the class of 'light motor vehicle' as provided in Section 10(2)(d) is competent to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7,500 kg."

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., AIR 2017 SC 3668
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. So far as the contention of the appellant that a separate endorsement on the licence is required to drive a transport light motor vehicle is concerned, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:333 3 MA-168-2010 the case of Mukund Dewangan (supra), this Court does not find any substance on merits in this regard.
The Claims Tribunal has rightly held the Insurance Company to pay the compensation to the claimant and thereafter recover the same from owner and driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly, no interference is warranted in the impugned award passed by the Claims Tribunal.
10. In view of the foregoing discussion, the instant miscellaneous appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *AVI*
